jordan (Customer): Hey @marie, running into intermittent failures when using structured output / JSON mode. Our client tries to parse the API response with pydantic and zod; sometimes pydantic raises 'value is not a valid dict' and zod says 'Unexpected end of input'. Request id: req-0a1b2c3. This started after we migrated a prompt to model-redwood/v2. Any ideas?

marie (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (request + full response body) and let us know if you're using streaming? Also which validators/versions?

jordan (Customer): Not streaming. Here's a stripped repro (curl):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"model-redwood/v2","json_mode":true,"prompt":"Generate JSON: {\\"user\\": \"name\\"}"}'
```

And the raw response body we got (copied exactly):

```
"Here's the result:
{
  \"user\": {
    \"name\": \"alice\",
  },
  \"id\": 12345

"
```

As you can see there's extra commentary and a trailing comma + missing closing brace. pydantic error: `TypeError: value is not a valid dict (type=type_error.dict)`; zod error: `Unexpected end of input (at 56)`

marie (Support): OK thanks — two likely issues: (1) model is emitting free-form commentary before/after the JSON, and (2) malformed JSON (trailing comma / missing brace). We'll need the full request id and timestamp to look up logs; you gave req-0a1b2c3 which helps. Can you also confirm the exact schema you passed to the API (if any)?

jordan (Customer): We used a JSON schema in the prompt wrapper (we pass `json_schema` in our client):

```
{"type":"object","properties":{"user":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}},"id":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["user","id"]}
```

daniel (Eng): @marie / @vika — I pulled the server logs for req-0a1b2c3. The model output stream includes a preface line: `Here's the result:` and then the JSON partial you pasted. The tokenizer split triggered the end-of-sequence before a closing brace in a few cases. Looks like v2 has slightly different generation behavior for our structured prompt templates.

vika (ML): This is model-driven schema drift — model sometimes emits natural language and can include trailing punctuation. Two mitigation paths: (A) force a stricter generation constraint using our `response_format: {type: "json_schema", schema: ...}` envelope so the model is primed to emit pure JSON, or (B) implement server-side normalization that extracts the first balanced JSON object. We already have heuristics but they fail on trailing comma.

marie (Support): For immediate customer workaround: try adding `stop_sequences: ["\n\n"]` and/or set `response_format.type` to `json_schema` if your SDK supports it. Also we can enable a server-side tolerant parser for your org (coerce_trailing_commas=true) while we fix the root cause. Would you like us to enable that for your account?

jordan (Customer): Yes please enable the tolerant parser — that would unblock us quickly. Also can you share a long-term fix? We rely heavily on pydantic validation in backend so we need stable, parseable JSON.

daniel (Eng): I opened an internal ticket to add an explicit parse-error envelope on API responses when structured parsing fails. New behavior: instead of returning raw broken text, API will return HTTP 422 with body `{ "error_type": "structured_parse_error", "raw_output": "...", "parse_hint": "trailing_comma" }`. This should make client-side handling deterministic. We'll roll a canary later today.

vika (ML): Also pushing a model-prompt tweak for model-redwood/v2 to bias it toward pure JSON emission for `json_schema` requests. We'll run evals against our prompt set to ensure regression doesn't reintroduce commentary.

ops-bot: deploy/canary started by daniel — canary-id=canary-2026-03-17-17

marie (Support): Done — I enabled the tolerant parser for your org id: org-9012. Can you retest and paste the result?

jordan (Customer): Retested. Parser accepted the response and our pydantic model passes now. Thanks! Please keep me updated on the canary. :tada:

daniel (Eng): Canary shows ~0.6% parse_failures on a small traffic slice vs 2.4% before — rolling to 20% now. I'll post an update to #eng-runtime when we start broader rollout.

marie (Support): Glad that helped. If you hit anything else, ping us with the new request id. Closing this thread for now. :white_check_mark:
